This is a monumental achievement in gaming. Not only does it look like a brand new game but it launched without a hitch. The industry needs to study under Rockstar's coders because this game is so well optimized that it makes recent AAA releases look damn embarassing. This is without a doubt one of the greatest games ever created.______Gameplay+ Almost 100% a completely succesful port.+ The mouse control for Airplanes and Helicopters is surprisingly succesful once you get used to it.+ The First Person view is also splendidly well integrated and fun to switch in and out of. I still found myself wanting to play this with a gamepad because it does have it's spikes of difficulty where auto aim toggling/target toggling+ Modible cars and bikes. Although I wish the default cars for each character were able to be changed. Some aspects of the modibiltiy leave a little be desired and seem to be more cosmetic than functional.+ Character stats that improve with usage. Always a + to have a little RPG element to an action game. This causes me to drive Motorcycles at top speeds againsts 3 lanes of highway traffic to level up Driving. Like Trinity.Graphics+ Amazingly gorgeous improvement from the PS3/XBOX version. HD textures FTW.+ Features like NVIDIA TXAA PCSS Ambient Occlusion Depth of Field are well implemented.+ Incredibly well coded and optimized to run well on high settings with an average machine. No PhysX (. Dead by Daylight is a game I've put a LOT of time into since its release and always end up coming back to despite its rough edges. The asymmetrical multiplayer/horror genre of game is pretty niche and while there have been a few other attempts at it none have really taken off like this game has. I was pretty excited when it first released and despite it's horrendously buggy and unbalanced debut it was a blast. I mean at that point nobody really knew what they were doing anyway.The gist of the game is 4 survivor players try to repair generators scattered around the map to open the exit gate while a killer player hunts them down in an attempt to ritually sacrifice them. There are a wide variety of killers with different playstyles to choose from and while the differences between survivors are largely cosmetic there are a wide variety of perks and abilities you can unlock to change up your playstyle a bit as well as good map variety.However while the game has come a long way it can still seem a bit unpolished at times. It can still be a bit buggy especially with graphical glitches but it's rarely anything that ruins the game. The balance is also hit or miss but honestly it's probably better now than at any point in the past. It's not really a competitive game at heart anyway despite the ranking system. But on the flip side that means that play at higher ranks between veteran players is where a lot of the balance issues become glaringly obvious. But that's a whole other discussion in and of itself.To be honest the biggest turnoff would probably be the community but that could be said for a lot of online games. But due to the nature of the game with it's opposing roles both "killer" and "survivor" mains constantly antagonize each other. I play and enjoy both sides personally so my advice would just be to ignore whatever negativity your opponents try to berate you with and play the game how you want. It also helps that you can choose to just hide the post game chat completely and all the salt that comes with it. This game can be a bit hard for new players to get into especially once they start playing against players with a bit more experience as there's a lot of meta tactics that you might not be aware of that can make the game seem quite frustrating if you don't know how to utilize/play against them. But once again I suppose that could be said for most online games.All in all there can be a bit of a learning curve and while the game can certainly feel frustrating at times it's still a unique game experience with tons of replay value especially if you like horror aesthetics of it.

There's no game remotely like it. If you measure the merit of a game simply by how many hours you're likely to play then Rocket League is right up there you're likely to get sucked in and play for dozens of hours.But after a certain point it became a negative experience for me. The matchmaking system leaves a lot to be desired. Way too often I found myself in 3v3 matches with expert players who would run circles around me and other players running up the score. It's really not fun when that happens even when the ringer is on my own team. Maybe this is a quaint sentiment but I usually play games to have fun and surmount a reasonable level of challenge not drive myself crazy trying to become a ninja master at them.The community can also be toxic but I guess you ll get that in most MMOs especially when the player base mushrooms. Most players are friendly but a minority are not. If you want to play for hundreds of hours in order to get good that s certainly your prerogative. But if you then criticize your anonymous teammates for not being up to your level it makes you nothing more than an obnoxious a hole. That s not really Psyonix s fault but if I m being honest it still drives me crazy. I wish it didn t but I guess that s just human nature /Anyway maybe matchmaking can be fixed. I don t really know but I d like to see Psyonix at least try to address it.

This will be more of a ''my experience with this game'' type of review, because saying things like ''great gameplay'' will not suit something I've experienced with Counter-Strike. Here you go: I remember back in 2002 I was at a friend's house and he was playing a game. I didn't know the name of the game nor I had internet to find it. A few weeks passed by and another friend came over and he didn't have a computer, so he brought a disc with a game in it. He told me that it was one of the best games and from that very moment I knew that it is going to be the game I saw at the other friend's house. When I saw the Counter-Strike logo I was filled with gamegasm (?) and I was so happy. I don't remember a day when I was so happy like back then. So, the journey started. I was playing it hardcore. Made friends, clans, was involved in communities and even made two myself. Counter-Strike is my first game which I played competitively and it was a whole experience. Playing public servers and maybe some servers with mods was very fun, but playing it competitively made it very intense and stressful. In a pleasant way, ofcourse. Shooters these days try to be different, advanced in a way. Sometimes the most simple games like Counter-Strike are the ones that live to this day. Also, there are plenty of mods to keep your attention to this game. The gameplay is very simple - defend as a Counter-Terrorist, attack as a Terrorist to plant the bomb or save the hostages as a CT. I am sure most of you already know this and I doubt there are gamers that haven't heard or know the gameplay of Counter-Strike, so I am sharing here more of my experience. I wish I could find my CS Anthology account which I've lost since 2008. So, I decided I am going to buy this game again and here you go - more than a thousand hours played. I still play it from time to time to this day and it brings back many great memories and I sometimes even stumble upon people I've played with years ago. I think Counter-Strike changed gaming in a major way and we wouldn't have many games like we have today, if this game wouldn't exist. I am sure many of people already have played games like CS:GO, but never the roots. I doubt any of you will play it for more than an hour, because it's much more simple and it differs a lot in my opinion from CS:GO and modern games.

Despite many iterations, nothing quite plays like the original. It's not hard to see why there are still 10,000 to 60,000 people playing this at any one time on any day , fifteen years after launch and why it is always in the top ten games currently being played on all of Steam. The original days of Counter-Strike remain the most enjoyable gaming experiences of my entire life. It's unlikely that will ever be trumped.

Counter-Strike was an amazing achievement. A free mod for the original Half-Life that outshone it's parent game completely and become becoming incredibly popular, so popular in fact, that it was sold it stores as a individual entity back when it was still free to download for anyone that already owned Half-Life. Nowadays a mod turning into a full game is almost common place and happens sometimes even without the popularity but back then, it was a monumental accomplishment. Counter-Strike managed to become the most played PC shooter of all time and even to this day boasts both a strong competitive scene and tons of active public servers. How many other online shooters can say that their online community is still alive and kicking 12 years down the line? The game itself I never really cared much for, I played it back in the 5.2 beta days and although there is something to admire about the simplistic purity of it's gameplay this has never been the kind of game I could really get stuck into. The developers tried to introduce a number of new game-modes back in the beta days but quickly found that trying to complicate the game would only leave the players confused and unsure of how to proceed. Counter-Strike is a simplistic teamshooter but it is a milestone in gaming history and one that we should be happy and proud of because Counter-Strike's simple existence is the reason why modding turned mainstream.
